content.text: {"title":"The Courtyard Wind-Up Show","premise":"In a sunny courtyard, three children prepare a puppet play for a promised audience. A sudden breeze tangles the curtain, timid puppeteer Nia wants a tiny safe role, and ambitious stage manager Bo wants a grand finale. Depending on what they first notice and believe, the children may create a kite-puppet rescue, an intimate shadow show, or a wildly improvised weather parade.","cast_and_props":"Mara (child, wants the audience delighted), Nia (child, timid puppeteer who wants to perform without being stared at), Bo (child, ambitious stage manager who wants a spectacular finale), and Puck (small paper puppet). Props: courtyard stage, curtain, spool of blue ribbon, paper sun, basket of cloud puppets, and a low stool. State keys begin with existing entities: mara, nia, bo, puck, curtain, ribbon, sun, clouds, stool, stage.","kernels_and_interactions":"1) Observe/tell: Mara observes curtain.tangled or Nia's quiet request; Nia can tell Bo she wants a shadow performance. Knowledge enables the correct response rather than mind-reading. 2) Ownership/trade: Mara owns the blue ribbon; transferring it to Bo or Nia changes who can solve or redesign the show. 3) Performance: a child performs a concrete style (kite_rescue, shadow_story, or weather_parade), changing stage.performance and audience.response. 4) Physical rearrangement: curtain, sun, clouds, stool, and ribbon acquire concrete locations or states. 5) Social agreement: the children agree to a small role or invite the courtyard audience close. Reuse greeting, ribbon transfer, and final bow scenes across paths, with different preceding discoveries and resulting performances.","seed_parameters":"Seed initializes three actual conditions: curtain.tangled (true/false), nia.brave (0/1), and bo.plan (quiet/ grand). Additional initial properties include mara.invited_audience, ribbon.owner, and clouds.location. Openings are individually guarded: a tangled curtain establishes the breeze problem; a timid Nia establishes the conflicting-wants problem; an ambitious Bo establishes the mistaken-assumption problem when he believes the audience wants a huge finale. Vary at least two premise keys per seed so the same scene can carry different meaning.","candidate_scenes":"12–18 candidates: greet_audience; observe_tangled_curtain; observe_nia_quiet; observe_bo_plan; tell_nia_to_mara; tell_mara_to_bo; transfer_ribbon_to_bo; transfer_ribbon_to_nia; untangle_curtain_with_ribbon; fold_curtain_into_shadow_screen; place_sun_high; place_clouds_low; invite_audience_close; agree_small_role; perform_kite_rescue; perform_shadow_story; perform_weather_parade; bow_and_share_paper_sun. The three consequence sets are: (A) ribbon catches the curtain and Puck becomes a flying kite-puppet, earning a cheering audience; (B) the curtain becomes a shadow screen, Nia performs behind it, and the audience sits close and quiet; (C) Bo's grand plan turns into a comic weather parade, with clouds, sun, and children crossing the courtyard together. Each performance changes stage.performance and audience.response, satisfying a goal requiring an actual performance plus response.","constraints":"Declare every slot before use; all values scalar and keys rooted in physical entities. Use 3–5 kernel families, prune=True, 5–10 selected events, and only 1–2 pivotal scenes (likely agree_small_role and invite_audience_close). No abstract counters. Every observe/tell must enable a later guarded action. Every performance must be reachable and narratively described only after its event. Openings and scene cards condition all variable claims; no invented repairs, audience reactions, or unused prop actions. premise_keys: curtain.tangled, nia.brave, bo.plan, ribbon.owner. outcome_keys: stage.performance, audience.response, nia.content. Goal requires stage.performance in a completed set and audience.response == delighted (or quietly_charmed for the shadow path).","different_endings":"Kite-rescue: Puck sails above the curtain while the blue ribbon hums, and the courtyard claps in a rhythm like little wings. Shadow-story: the curtain glows with Nia's paper hands; afterward, the audience leaves the stool in a neat moon-shaped circle around her. Weather-parade: Bo marches under the paper sun with cloud puppets bobbing behind him, while Mara's once-serious stage becomes a cheerful wandering sky. Each ending gets at least two variants, guarded by the actual stage.performance and audience.response values."}
